entity_failure_rule.rule: For any entity with at least two human item-level units, the classifier must not miss all of them.

comparison_with_protocol_2_1.interpretation: Fine-grained agreement improved modestly relative to protocol 2.1.0, but independent item-level recall fell from 28.57% to 14.29%. Protocol 2.2.0 therefore does not resolve the M4-gating under-detection problem.

development_to_validation_contrast.interpretation: The large improvement observed on previously human-labelled development data did not generalize to the preregistered unseen ecological sample. The independent VAL-007 result is authoritative for validation status.

diagnostic_findings: BBC is the only strong entity-level cluster in this validation: 5 of 6 fine-grained roles were exact and both human audiovisual items were detected.

Observation-root fallback over-predicts homepage for semantically richer roots and filtered archive surfaces, including BNT archive, Cinemateca Digital, HENRI, Ninateka and Memoryscapes archive surfaces.

All five human audiovisual_item pages under Cinémathèque française HENRI were predicted institutional_landing_page, indicating that descendant institutional-root logic dominates item specificity on this architecture.
Both human audiovisual_item Cinemateca Portuguesa Ficha pages were predicted unknown, despite item-specific ficha URLs and public Vimeo media in the collected context.
All four human audiovisual_item Memoryscapes clip pages were predicted unknown despite clip-specific routes and detected public MP4/Vimeo media.
Search/index recognition remains weak: only 1 of 9 human search_or_index surfaces was classified exactly, while six were predicted homepage.
Access-state inference agreed with the human reference on all 31 units, supporting continued separation of access state from semantic surface role.
The development-only gains of protocol 2.2.0 on previously labelled units did not generalize to this independent sample, so no tuning conclusion may be drawn from CAL-006 as independent evidence.
sample_composition_notes: All six preregistered entities are represented in the final 31-unit review queue.
FINA/Ninateka contributed only one eligible observed surface under the preregistered deterministic discovery and exclusion rules. No replacement entity or post-hoc substitution was used.

acceptance_assessment.rationale: Weighted F1 was 0.2828 against the preregistered 0.50 minimum; every human class with support >=5 had recall below 0.50; binary item-level recall was 14.29% against the 70% minimum; and three entities with at least two human item-level units had all such units missed. Access agreement was 100% but cannot compensate for semantic or item-level failure.

scientific_decision: Do not accept protocol 2.2.0 as independently validated for fine-grained M3 surface typing and do not scale M4. Preserve VAL-007 unchanged as the authoritative independent result. Retain access-state separation. Any classifier or sampling improvement must be implemented under a later protocol version and evaluated with a new preregistered, prediction-frozen independent ecological validation before M4 scaling can be reconsidered.
limitations: The independent ecological sample contains 31 units from six entities and is too small for broad generalisation.
FINA/Ninateka contributed only one review unit, limiting entity-level interpretation for that corpus.

Homepage, news_or_editorial, item_record and restricted_or_unavailable had zero human support; institutional_landing_page and unknown had support of one. Performance claims for sparse classes are descriptive only.
Within-entity route repetition is substantial, especially the five HENRI film pages and four Memoryscapes clip pages, so aggregate metrics are sensitive to clustered architecture patterns.
The sample was not designed to estimate prevalence of surface classes.
Human labels are authoritative for this blind validation and were frozen before model predictions were opened; they must not be retroactively revised using model output.
The preregistered thresholds are operational project gates, not population-level confidence intervals or prevalence estimates.
prohibited_interpretations: does not estimate corpus-wide prevalence of surface classes
does not validate protocol 2.2.0 for fine-grained surface typing
100% item-level precision does not compensate for 14.29% recall and the entity all-miss failures
100% access-state agreement does not compensate for semantic surface-role or item-level failure
does not modify the official T2 baseline
does not establish corpus membership, institutional AI use or AI participation in audiovisual content
development-set performance from CAL-006 must not be reported as independent validation evidence
